text:
Leah (PM): quick sync — customer X is pushing to get the dynamic-routing SLA in Q2. they want 99.9% for served requests. can we ship a minimal version or is this going to eat SRE cycles?
Alex P.: short answer: depends on rollback/fallbacks. current runtime has partial fallback but not route-level SLAs.
Maria K.: if we promise 99.9 we need automated fallback to hosted model variant + alerts. otherwise oncall will drown. :grimacing:
Jamal (oncall): +1. Last sprint we had 3 pages from a single routing change. toil spike was ~8h to triage. we should avoid manual runbooks for the initial launch.
Chris - EngProd: what if we scope launch to "best-effort" routing but with a canary policy and a static cap per customer? lets get something out and iterate.
Leah (PM): thinking tradeoff between velocity vs reliability. we can either 1) remove SLA from public launch and roll SLA in enterprise / dedicated, or 2) keep SLA but shrink initial feature set. thoughts?
Alex P.: propose RICE-ish quick score to decide. small table we can use in thread:
```
Option A: Launch v1 no SLA, canary routing
Reach: 6
Impact: 5
Confidence: 7
Effort: 3
RICE ~ (6*5*7)/3 = 70

Option B: Launch v1 with SLA + automated fallback
Reach: 6
Impact: 8
Confidence: 5
Effort: 8
RICE ~ (6*8*5)/8 = 30
```
Maria K.: that math aligns with risk posture. Option A reduces toil but we need clear marketing language. customers X and Y might balk tho.
Jamal (oncall): plus operational run rate: Option B adds ~2 FTE-months of work for rollout automation and extra test harness. if we don't have that, pages go up.
Chris - EngProd: alternative hybrid: gated SLA for high-paying customers only (Dedicated / Private), and public API gets best-effort until we complete rollout automation. reduces risk and keeps product motion.
Leah (PM): that's leaning Enterprise-first for SLA. we can add explicit launch criteria:
- Automated fallback present and exercised in canary
- Rollout needs A/B circuit breaker with 5m cooldown
- Runbook auto-generated from playbook templates
- MTTx target for routing failures < 15m for canary
If we can't hit those by code freeze, public launch is best-effort.
Alex P.: I like explicit criteria. also add cost guardrail: quantization/cache configs validated so we don't blow token budget in canaries.
Maria K.: we'll need a short spike to prove rollback automation. suggest 2-week spike, deliverables: `rollback-lambda` + unit test + synthetic canary.
Jamal (oncall): ok for oncall coverage during spike, but schedule needs to avoid two-weekend rotations.
Leah (PM): decision: run 2-week spike to implement automated fallback and rollback tests. if spike succeeds, we enable SLA for dedicated/customers only on first launch. public API stays best-effort until full automation.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled spike branch deploy to staging at 2024-06-05T18:00Z (job #4921).
Alex P.: I'll create a short RFC with the RICE numbers + the launch criteria and link to this thread. will @Leah ping stakeholders when RFC is up.
Leah (PM): thanks everyone. small follow-ups: @Maria K. own spike plan, @Jamal block oncall gaps, @Chris draft ent packaging for Dedicated SLAs.
Maria K.: will do.
Jamal (oncall): acknowledged.
Chris - EngProd: drafting now. :rocket:
Leah (PM): closing thread — we'll reconvene after spike demo. :white_check_mark:
